messages:
olivia-newhire: Hey team — quick benefits Q from my first week. I submitted a life event (marriage) in Workday on 2024-07-16 and asked to add my spouse. I got a confirmation that benefits were added 8/1, but our wedding date was 2024-07-15. Is it possible to have coverage retroactive to the marriage date? Also I picked up a prescription on 2024-07-20 — can that be reimbursed if the carrier approves a retro effective date?

jessica-peopleops: Hey @olivia-newhire welcome! Congrats 🎉 Generally carriers will either backdate to the life event date or to the 1st of the next month. It depends on the insurance carrier and timing. I've created a ticket with the benefits team to escalate — please upload your marriage cert + spouse ID to the benefits portal so we have docs on file: https://benefits.redwood.internal/claims (internal).

ryan-hr: @jessica correct. Also @olivia-newhire can you DM me the Workday ticket #? If the carrier will backdate we can request a letter of retroactive coverage from them. For the prescription: what was the Rx and amount?

olivia-newhire: Ticket ID is 84211. The prescription was Lisinopril 10mg filled 2024-07-20 at CVS, $12.48. I have the paper receipt (photo).

jessica-peopleops: Perfect — thanks. Two paths here: (1) If carrier approves the retro date they will process the pharmacy claim normally (you may need to resubmit the receipt to the carrier if it was paid out-of-pocket). (2) If carrier denies retro coverage, People Ops can process a one-time manual reimbursement. For the manual route we need: pharmacy receipt, marriage certificate, and a short note explaining the dates. Submit those to Expensify/Concur with the expense code "benefits-one-time".

payroll-bot: FYI: Manual reimbursements processed through payroll may be taxable depending on how they are paid. For pre-tax carrier claims, tax does not apply. See policy: /policies/benefits/reimbursements and reach out to payroll for tax specifics.

alex-peopleops: If we go payroll route, it usually shows up as 'Other Compensation' on the paystub and may take 1–2 pay cycles to appear. We can request expedited processing but can't guarantee same-paycheck.

olivia-newhire: Got it — thanks. If carrier approves retro, do I need to resubmit the Rx claim to them or will People Ops do that?

ryan-hr: Carrier typically wants the member (you) to file the claim first. Once you have the retro effective date we can generate a confirmation letter from HR to attach. I'll DM you step-by-step carrier submission instructions and the carrier claim portal link.

jessica-peopleops: I'll update ticket 84211 as soon as I hear back from benefits. tagging @olivia-newhire @ryan-hr — we'll follow up here once we have carrier response.

olivia-newhire: Thank you all — really appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
